terms.comment: Greek ἐπίσκοπος, an overseer; Cicero once calls himself one, in Greek (Att. 7.11, Lewis & Short). The same word in East and West.

terms.gloss: a bishop; classically a high priest
terms.comment: Classically the overseer of a temple, a high priest (Cic., Liv.); the Christian writers use it of a bishop.

phrases.latin: et vēnī Mediōlānium ad Ambrosium episcopum
phrases.english: and I came to Milan, to Ambrose the bishop

episcopus.against: Lewis & Short ĕpīscŏpus, taking the heavy syllable for a long vowel
episcopus.html: Greek ἐπίσκοπος, from ἐπί, with short ι, and σκοπός. Lewis & Short leave the i unmarked in their own compounds chōrĕpiscŏpus, cŏĕpiscŏpus and pseudŏĕpiscŏpus.
